Brazil Fisheries Sector Hit by Widespread Worker Walkout

A coordinated walkout by fisheries workers in Brazil has brought significant disruptions across the country’s fisheries industry, with processing plants, coastal fleet operations, and aquaculture facilities reporting work stoppages since Monday. The strike, led by the National Federation of Fisheries Workers (FNTP), centers on demands for improved wages, enhanced safety protocols, and better health coverage.

As of Wednesday, industry sources confirm that over 65% of the sector’s active workforce is participating in the action, affecting operations in major hubs such as Itajaí, Belém, and Santos. Plants operated by firms including Maré Alta Pescados and Oceano Vivo report halted production lines and idle cold storage facilities. “Our plant has been forced to suspend all processing activities since the strike began,” said Paulo Ferraz, operations manager at Maré Alta Pescados’ Itajaí facility. “We have raw fish inventory building up and are unable to ship products as scheduled.”

Fishing fleets in the states of Pará and Santa Catarina are largely docked, with only skeletal crews maintaining vessels. According to a statement from FNTP President Luciana Barreto, “Our members are united in their call for fair compensation and improved safety standards, especially after a year marked by increased accidents and illness.”

The walkout’s effects are being felt at aquaculture sites as well. At AquaVerde in Espírito Santo, maintenance and feeding routines are being performed by a reduced team of supervisors, while regular staff remain off duty. “We’re concerned about the potential impact on fish health and quality if this continues,” said a company spokesperson.

Fisheries industry analysts warn that prolonged disruption may lead to significant losses in output and create operational backlogs. “If the strike extends into next week, the sector could see a 40% reduction in processed volume for June,” said Gabriel Nogueira, fisheries market analyst at Setorial Insights.

Negotiations between union leaders and the Fisheries Industry Employers Association are ongoing. Both sides have signaled willingness to find common ground, but as of press time, no agreement had been reached. FNTP said the strike will continue until satisfactory offers are made.
